why: Both govern neighbour relations in the same material, so border negotiation and help given to neighbours are hard to separate.

why.T3-010: The item's dominant practice is negotiating boundaries and shared space with neighbouring works; also at floor: T3-011, T3-122, T3-139, T3-072, T3-194, T3-024, T3-195, T3-149.

why.T3-005: This is an active-attack defence thread: alarms, reports of ground lost, calls to hold and fight back, so it stays with T3-005 rather than repair or tracing.

why.T3-105: The item is about preserving the finished mural through a timelapse and an enlarged cut-out, matching T3-105 rather than celebration or crediting.

why.T3-041: The item extends the Mass Effect composition by proposing and adding Garrus, the Andromeda Initiative symbol, and other pieces beside N7.
why.T3-055: Several concepts add borders or boxes to completed work specifically to protect it from takeover, which is not carried by T3-041 alone.

multiplacement_log.why_not_one: T3-041 carries the added pieces and enlargement but not the explicit protective border/box practice.
multiplacement_log.why_this_one: T3-055's gate is satisfied by boxing creations and adding left-side borders so Garrus is preserved.
multiplacement_log.dispensable: Drop T3-055 if forced; the item would lose the protection-against-takeover aspect.

why.T3-073: The concepts are retrospective reports of what happened to the work, including destruction, reformation, and local battles, rather than fresh repair or celebration.

why.T3-117: The exchange hopes the canvas event will return, which is a bare hope at the end rather than a concrete plan to carry work to a later canvas.

why.T3-022: The item is the repeated practice of relocating and rebuilding after a wipe or contested spot, not only weighing the move.

why.T3-088: Using old alts in different browsers to speed placements is exactly placing beyond the one-pixel limit by extra accounts.

why.T3-010: The item's dominant practice is negotiating boundaries and shared space with neighbouring works; also at floor: T3-011, T3-122, T3-139, T3-072, T3-194, T3-024, T3-195, T3-149.

why.T3-038: The larger share is first-time placing and building the outpost, Garrus and N7, with models and coordinates for the build.
why.T3-021: Several concepts are specifically keeping pixels clean, repairing troll changes, and maintaining the mark, which T3-038 alone would not carry.

multiplacement_log.why_not_one: T3-038 carries the building and progress but not the explicit cleaning and repair-maintenance practice.
multiplacement_log.why_this_one: T3-021's gate is satisfied by keeping N7 clean, repairing changed blocks, and maintaining after migrations.
multiplacement_log.dispensable: Drop T3-021 if forced; the item would lose the repair-and-clean upkeep aspect.

why.T3-005: The concepts are dominated by defence and holding against attacks on N7 and Garrus.
why.T3-002: There are also distinct calls to start, build, and finish the marks with no attack in view.

multiplacement_log.why_not_one: T3-005 carries the defensive rally but not the initial build/finish recruitment calls.
multiplacement_log.why_this_one: T3-002's gate is satisfied by calls to make the mark, help make N7, and finish the work.
multiplacement_log.dispensable: Drop T3-002 if forced; the item would lose the build-and-finish call aspect.

why.T3-009: Most concepts celebrate the finished SG/BM murals and the shared result.
why.T3-043: Several concepts separately credit designers, builders, the starter, and the defending team.

multiplacement_log.why_not_one: T3-009 carries the celebration but not the named credit to makers and defenders.
multiplacement_log.why_this_one: T3-043's gate is satisfied by crediting designers/builders and thanking the project starter.
multiplacement_log.dispensable: Drop T3-043 if forced; the item would lose the specific maker-credit aspect.

why.T3-127: The pair asks and encourages showing the canvas work to the SG staff, i.e. seeking the represented creators' notice.

why.T3-040: The second exchange is an apology and offer to redraw a neighbour's overwritten character, matching T3-040.
why.T3-170: The first exchange separately treats apparent blocking as mistaken friendly help and then identifies and forgives it, satisfying T3-170.

multiplacement_log.why_not_one: T3-040 carries the apology and repair offer but not the mistaken-help/vandalism recognition.
